orientation.batter_faces: DUE NORTH. Unusually for an MLB park, Petco Park is aligned almost exactly on the compass: the batter at home plate looks due north toward center field. Consequences that the sources state directly: home plate sits at the SOUTH end of the site (the main entrance behind home plate is at the south end of Park Boulevard); the THIRD-BASE side and LEFT FIELD are on the WEST side of the building and get shade first; the FIRST-BASE side and RIGHT FIELD are on the EAST side and stay sunny longest; the sun sets behind the third-base grandstand.
orientation.source: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petco_Park - 'Unlike many outdoor ballparks, in which the batter faces northeast, at Petco the batter faces due north, and fans in the grandstands are treated to a view of San Diego Bay and the San Diego skyline beyond the left field seats, as well as a view of Balboa Park, which contains the San Diego Zoo, beyond center field.' INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED by RateYourSeats' shade guide: 'Petco Park faces north, so the sun will set behind sections on the third base side of the field. These sections - labeled with even numbers - will be shaded long before seats on the first base side.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/petco-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats), and by a RateYourSeats expert answer referring to 'the outer west wall of the ballpark' as the thing the sun eventually falls behind. ALSO corroborated by the reason for the alignment: Petco Park Insider, on the Western Metal Supply Co. building, 'In fact, the ballpark was built around the building to accommodate it, designed from the building outward and even repositioned slightly toward the north (instead of the more common north-east).' (https://www.petcoparkinsider.com/western-metal-supply-building). GATE GEOGRAPHY CROSS-CHECK (independent, symmetric about home plate): Petco Park Insider lists the Home Plate Gate at 'Park Blvd. and Tony Gwynn Drive / Southeast side of stadium'; the Gaslamp Gate at 'Seventh Ave. and K St. / Northwest side / Near the Western Metal Supply Co. Building' (i.e. left field / 3rd base); and the East Village Gate at '10th Avenue and K Street / Northeast side' (right field) (https://www.petcoparkinsider.com/petco-park-entry-gates). Northwest = left field = third base = even sections; northeast = right field = first base = odd sections. This matches the batter-faces-north statement exactly.

numbering_direction.summary: *** PETCO PARK DOES NOT USE A SINGLE MONOTONIC NUMBERING SWEEP. IT NUMBERS CENTER-OUT WITH AN ODD/EVEN SPLIT. *** The rule, stated in almost exactly these words by three independent sources including an OFFICIAL Padres page: ODD-NUMBERED SECTIONS ARE ON THE FIRST-BASE SIDE AND CONTINUE INTO RIGHT FIELD; EVEN-NUMBERED SECTIONS ARE ON THE THIRD-BASE SIDE AND CONTINUE INTO LEFT FIELD. Numbers therefore INCREASE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE, starting from a small centred group behind home plate and running outward along both foul lines simultaneously. Any generator that assumes 'numbers increase toward first base' OR 'numbers increase toward third base' will be wrong for half the ballpark. Per-series detail, all sourced below in 'anchors': (a) FIELD-LEVEL DUGOUT / CLUB SERIES 0-13 (single- and double-digit sections, sold as Blue Shield Home Plate Club, First Base VIP Box and Third Base Coach's Box). Section 0 and 1-6 are the Home Plate Club directly behind the plate; within that group section 5 is the first-base end ('Section 5 will be closest to the Padres dugout and on-deck circle') and section 6 the third-base end ('Section 6 sits closer to the visiting team's on-deck circle'). Then ODD 7, 9, 11, 13 run out along the FIRST-BASE line (First Base VIP Box = 7, 9, 11; section 13 is a small 3-row section further out) and EVEN 8, 10 run out along the THIRD-BASE line (Third Base Coach's Box). There is NO section 12 in this run (see 'uncertain'). (b) FIELD LEVEL / 100 SERIES 101-137. 101-106 are the centred Field Box VIP group directly behind home plate, with 101 and 102 the most centred. Then ODD 107, 109, 111, 113 are first-base infield; ODD 115, 117, 119, 121, 123, 125, 127 continue down the first-base line; ODD 129, 131, 133, 135, 137 are the right-field 'Home Run' sections (137 is the outermost right-field section - there is NO 136). EVEN 108, 110, 112, 114 are third-base infield; EVEN 116, 118, 120, 122, 124 continue down the third-base line (124 sits at the left-field foul pole next to Pacifico Porch); EVEN 126, 128, 130, 132, 134 are the left-field 'Home Run' sections, with 134 immediately beside the bullpens in left-center. (c) TOYOTA TERRACE / 200 SERIES 201-224 plus UPPER BOX OUTFIELD 226-235. RateYourSeats states it outright for this level: 'Odd-numbered sections run along the first base side' / 'Even-numbered sections run along the third base side'. Terrace VIP 201-204 sit directly behind home plate; Terrace Infield 205-210 above the dugouts; Terrace Reserved 211-217 farther down the lines; Terrace Pavilion 218-224 (Petco Park Insider extends this to 225) near the outfield corners. Beyond that, EVEN 226, 228, 230 are Upper Box LEFT FIELD ('Section 226 is at the foul pole and Western Metal Bldg, Section 230 is near the bullpen') and ODD 227, 229, 231, 233, 235 are Upper Box RIGHT FIELD ('Section 227 is at the Right Field foul pole, 235 closest to the center'). (d) UPPER DECK / 300 SERIES 300-329. Same split. 300-305 are the centred group behind home plate (section 300 carries RateYourSeats' 'Home Plate View' insight). EVEN 306-328 run toward third base and left field (section 328 'sits beside the historic Western Metal Supply building', i.e. the left-field corner; section 314 is 'along the 3rd base line'). ODD 307-329 run toward first base and right field (RateYourSeats' shade guide names 'Upper Deck in Right Field: Odd sections 315-329'; section 309 is beside the Stone Brewing Beer Garden). (e) *** THE ONE EXCEPTION: THE LETTERED PREMIER CLUB A-L. *** This is the only lettered seating run in the ballpark and it is NOT center-out - it is a single continuous sweep behind home plate that runs A -> L from the THIRD-BASE END to the FIRST-BASE END, with F and G dead centre. So for the lettered series alone, LETTERS INCREASE TOWARD FIRST BASE. Two independent sources agree: RateYourSeats ('Sections L and K will be closest to the Padres dugout' / 'Sections A and B sit closer to the visitor dugout'; the Padres dugout is on first base) and Petco Park Insider ('Section A is above 106, toward the third base side of Home Plate. Then wrapping alphabetically, F & G are dead center behind home plate, Section L is behind 105 on the 1st base side.'), plus a RateYourSeats fan review on Section L reading 'First base side. Lined up with home plate.'

numbering_direction.confidence: VERY HIGH for the odd/even split itself. Four independent source families agree and none dissents: (1) OFFICIAL - mlb.com/padres/ballpark/netting says in one sentence 'angled net coverage is from Sections 111-115 on the first base side and Sections 112-116 on the 3rd base side'; (2) RateYourSeats zone pages (Toyota Terrace states the rule outright; Field Box VIP, Home Plate Club, First Base VIP Box, Third Base Coach's Box, Lower Level Outfield and the shade guide all corroborate it); (3) Petco Park Insider states it as a park-wide rule and then enumerates every 100-level section on each side; (4) A View From My Seat's section-314 tags and left/right navigation. No source anywhere places an odd section on the third-base side or an even section on the first-base side. HIGH but slightly lower for the Premier Club lettered direction (A = third base, L = first base): two independent sources (RateYourSeats and Petco Park Insider) plus one fan review, but no official Padres statement. MEDIUM for the exact centred section within each tier (101 vs 102, 201 vs 202, 300 vs 301) - sources name the centred GROUP confidently but rarely the single most-centred section.

dugouts.home: FIRST BASE SIDE (the odd-numbered side, the east side of the ballpark). Ballparks of Baseball Facts & Figures states it flatly: '-Home Dugout: First Base' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/petco-park/). Corroborated four more times, independently: (1) RateYourSeats Field Box VIP - 'Sections 107-109 sit closest to the Padres dugout' and 'Row 8 in Section 107 sits directly behind the Padres dugout'; (2) RateYourSeats First Base VIP Box - 'Near the Padres Dugout: Positioned directly beside the Padres dugout, offering up-close views of players.' and 'The First Base VIP Box is located along the first base line at field level, sitting just beside the Padres dugout at Petco Park.'; (3) RateYourSeats section-107 page - Section Insight 'Near Padres Dugout', Seating Note 'These seats are located behind the Padres dugout', fan feedback 'Row 8 is the first row behind the Padres dugout in Section 107.'; (4) Petco Park Insider - 'Note: Home team dugout is located in front of sections 107 and the visitors dugout is across the field on the 3rd base side, located in front of Sections 108.' and 'Located beside the San Diego Padres home dugout (1st base side)'. RateYourSeats' shade guide adds the throwaway confirmation 'If being on the first base side is important (this is the Padres side, after all) ...'.
dugouts.visiting: THIRD BASE SIDE (the even-numbered side, the west side of the ballpark). RateYourSeats Field Box VIP: 'Sections 108-110 sit closest to the visiting team dugout' and 'Row 8 in Section 108 sits directly behind the visitor dugout'. RateYourSeats section-108 page: Section Insight 'Top Pick for Visiting Team Fans'; Seating Note 'For baseball games, these seats are located behind the visitor dugout'; fan reviews 'Directly behind the visitors dugout 9 rows up.' and 'Perfect view over looking the visitors dug out.' RateYourSeats Third Base Coach's Box: 'The sections are also located near the visiting team dugout, allowing fans to see players entering and exiting the field between innings.' and 'While the Third Base Coach's Box sits near the visiting team dugout, the First Base VIP Box places fans beside the Padres dugout'. RateYourSeats also labels the whole third-base half as the visitor side: 'Seats along the third base side (Visitor Side) typically move into the shade earlier during afternoon games.' Petco Park Insider: 'Located beside the visiting team's away dugout (3rd base side)'. Home Plate Club direction statement agrees: 'Section 6 sits closer to the visiting team's on-deck circle' (6 = even = third base).

bullpens: BOTH BULLPENS ARE BEYOND THE OUTFIELD WALL IN LEFT-CENTER FIELD, STACKED, WITH THE VISITING BULLPEN BEHIND THE PADRES BULLPEN. This is a post-2013 configuration and older sources describe a different layout, so the history matters. HISTORY, Wikipedia verbatim: 'An unusual feature Petco Park once had was that the home team bullpen was located behind the center field wall while the bullpen for the visiting team was in foul territory in right field. However, both bullpens were moved behind the center field wall after modifications to the ballpark were made prior to the start of the 2013 season.' and 'In addition, the visiting team bullpen was moved from foul territory in right field to behind the left-center field wall, right behind where the Padres bullpen is.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petco_Park). OFFICIAL PADRES RELEASE announcing the change, verbatim: 'Construction will also include the relocation of the visitors' bullpen off the field, addressing a potential player safety risk.' / 'Additionally, at the deepest point in left center field, the fence will be moved in from 402 feet to 390 feet. That modification will alter the setup of the home bullpen and will allow for the visiting team's bullpen to be relocated to the area behind the home bullpen.' / 'The home bullpen will be reconfigured to allow for the visitors' bullpen to be relocated from the field to the area behind the home bullpen.' (https://www.mlb.com/news/padres-announce-changes-to-petco-park-dimensions-for-2013/c-39981076). SO: HOME (PADRES) BULLPEN IS THE FRONT/NEARER ONE; VISITING BULLPEN IS BEHIND IT. WHICH SECTIONS ARE ADJACENT: RateYourSeats' Lower Level Outfield expert review - 'The left field side has a number of other advantages, including being right next to the bullpens near Section 134' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/petco-park/seating/sections/134). Petco Park Insider - 'Section 134 is right next to the bullpen.' (https://www.petcoparkinsider.com/100-level). One level up, Petco Park Insider - 'Section 230 is near the bullpen' (https://www.petcoparkinsider.com/padres-toyota-terrace). A RateYourSeats fan-feedback note on section 134 gives a seat-level bearing: 'The Padres Bullpen is to the Left of Section 134 - Sit close to Seat 12 in Section 134 to be near the Padres bullpen. The visitor bullpen is located behind the Padres bullpen, also next to Section 134.' Another section-134 fan review: 'End of the row and section, right against the fence to the bullpen.' CONFLICT ON THE LEFT/RIGHT BEARING: TickPick says 'Both teams' bullpens are located in left-center field, just to the right of Section 134.' (https://www.tickpick.com/blog/san-diego-padres-seating-chart-with-seat-views) - the exact opposite word from the RateYourSeats fan note. Neither states a frame of reference, so the left/right bearing relative to section 134 is NOT reliably derivable; the adjacency to section 134 and the left-center-field position are agreed by everyone. Also relevant: Wikipedia notes 'On August 18, 2018, a statue of National League Saves Leader and longtime Padre Trevor Hoffman was unveiled along K Street behind the bullpen, facing Gwynn's statue.'

accessibility.summary: The Padres publish an Accessibility Guide at https://www.mlb.com/padres/ballpark/disability-access-guide and repeat much of it in the Petco Park A-Z Guide at https://www.mlb.com/padres/ballpark/information/guide. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: unlike several other MLB clubs, THE PADRES DO NOT PUBLISH A PER-LEVEL LIST OF ACCESSIBLE / WHEELCHAIR SEATING SECTIONS. They publish seat CATEGORIES only, plus service locations by section. Verbatim on categories: 'The Padres have designated seats in Petco Park specifically for guests with disabilities in each of the following categories: Wheelchair Accessible, Semi-Ambulatory, and Transfer Seats.' / 'Wheelchair spaces are available for guests with disabilities who utilize a wheelchair.' / 'Semi-Ambulatory seats are available for guests with disabilities who require additional leg room beyond the minimum of twenty-four (24) inches traditional ballpark seating provides.' / 'Transfer seats are available for guests with disabilities who require an armless aisle seat.' Verbatim on elevators: 'Guests with disabilities have priority on all public elevators at Petco Park. Guests with disabilities can utilize a number of elevators located throughout Petco Park.' Verbatim on power: 'Electrical outlets for recharging wheelchairs and other necessary equipment are located in many seating areas designated for guests with disabilities.' Verbatim on lifts: 'Wheelchair Lifts are located throughout the ballpark to assist guests in accessing specific locations.' Verbatim on wheelchair escorts: 'Wheelchair escorts to and from seats are available upon request.' Verbatim on ALDs: 'The Padres are pleased to offer complimentary Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) to guests with hearing difficulties. ALDs can be obtained at the Guest Service Center located on the Field Level (Main Concourse) in Section 108.' Verbatim on sensory support: 'We are proud to partner with KultureCity and offer sensory bags at our Sensory Activation Vehicle in Park Blvd Plaza and Guest Services locations at 108, 131, 303.' Gates: 'All entry gates will open to guests 90 minutes prior to first pitch. Season Ticket Members have access to enter 2 hours prior to first pitch at two designated gates (Park Boulevard Gate and Home Plate Gate).' To buy accessible seats, Petco Park Insider records the phone route: 'To purchase accessible seating please call the Padres ticketing team at 619.795.5555.' The Padres netting page gives the same ticket-office number for seating questions: 'please contact the San Diego Padres ticket office at 619 795-5555.'
landmarks: ELEVATORS (official, verbatim): 'Elevators to access various ballpark levels are located near Sections 111, 114, 117, 137, 201, 217, 226, 235, 300, 311, 317, 314, 328, inside the Western Metal Supply Co. Building, as well as at the Gaslamp, East Village, Park Boulevard and Home Plate Gates. Please see a staff member for more information.' NOTE: the list is printed in that exact order on the official page, including the out-of-sequence '317, 314'. NOTE ALSO: the official list is LEVEL-AGNOSTIC - it does not say which elevator serves which level. Read against the odd/even rule it is a clean symmetric cross-check: 111 (odd, 1B) and 114 (even, 3B) and 117 (odd, 1B) and 137 (odd, RF corner) on the 100 level; 201 (centre), 217 (odd, 1B), 226 (even, LF corner) and 235 (odd, RF, nearest centre) on the 200 level; 300 (centre), 311/317 (odd, 1B/RF) and 314/328 (even, 3B/LF) on the 300 level; plus the Western Metal building (LF corner) and all four gates.

FIRST AID (official, verbatim): 'First Aid Stations are located in Sections 108 and 129. Trained medical personnel are on duty for all events to assist guests.' - one even/third-base, one odd/right-field.

SENSORY BAGS (official, verbatim): 'Sensory Activation Vehicle in Park Blvd Plaza and Guest Services locations at 108, 131, 303.'

Building'; 'Right Field / East Village Gate at 10th Avenue and K Street / Northeast side / Park Boulevard Gate at 10th Avenue'; 'Gallagher Square / Downtown Gate at Eighth Ave. and J St. / Northwest Side / Left-center field Balboa Park Gate at 9th Avenue and J St. / North side / Right-center field'. row_seat_conventions: ROWS - PREDOMINANTLY NUMBERS, with a small number of lettered front rows and at least one anomalous alphanumeric row. Petco Park Insider states the general rule verbatim: 'Row numbers:  Section rows start at 1 (closest to the field) and radiate back consecutively.' In practice RateYourSeats' per-section row labels show that MANY sections do NOT start at row 1, and several are split by a walkway. Observed labels, all verbatim from RateYourSeats section pages: FIELD-LEVEL DUGOUT SERIES - Section 13: 'Rows in Section 13 are labeled 1-3' (no entrance-row line). PREMIER CLUB (lettered sections) - Section A: 'Rows in Section A are labeled 1-10' (NO entrance-row line); Section L: 'Rows in Section L are labeled 1-16' (NO entrance-row line); the Premier Club zone page says 'Most Premier Club sections feature 15 rows of seating, though Sections F and G extend slightly deeper with about 20 rows.' 100 LEVEL - Section 101: 'Rows in Section 101 are labeled 8-20' + 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 20'; Section 102: '8-22' + entrance Row 22; Section 107: 'Rows in Section 107 are labeled 8-22, 26-40' + 'There is a walkway betweeen Rows 22 and 26' + entrance Row 40; Section 108: '8-22, 26-39' + walkway between 22 and 26 + entrance Row 39; Section 110: '5-22, 26-46' + walkway between 22 and 26 + entrance Row 42; Section 115: 'Rows in Section 115 are labeled 1-25, 1D, 27-44' + 'There is a walkway betweeen Rows 1D and 27' + entrance Row 44 (NOTE THE ANOMALOUS ROW '1D' SITTING BETWEEN ROWS 25 AND 27); Section 126: 'Rows in Section 126 are labeled A-B, 1-11' + entrance Row 11 (LETTERED ROWS A-B IN FRONT OF NUMBERED ROW 1); Section 128: 'Rows in Section 128 are labeled A-B, 1-11, BRS' + 'An entrance to this section is located at Row BRS' (NOTE THE ROW LABEL 'BRS' AT THE BACK - almost certainly a bar-rail/standing row); Section 129: '1-6, 7-25' + walkway between 6 and 7 + entrance Row 6; Section 133: '1-5, 7-25' + walkway between 5 and 7 + entrance Row 5; Section 134: '1-10' + entrance Row 10; Section 137: '1-6, 7-25' + walkway between 6 and 7 + entrance Row 6. 200 LEVEL - Section 201: 'Rows in Section 201 are labeled 1-8, 10' + 'There is a walkway betweeen Rows 8 and 10' + entrance Row 10; Section 204: '1-9' + entrance Row 9; Section 235: '1-25' + entrance Row 9; RateYourSeats' zone page says 'Each section has 15 rows or fewer' and Petco Park Insider says 'Sections on the Toyota Terrace level have a maximum of 15 rows.' 300 LEVEL - Section 300: 'Rows in Section 300 are labeled 5-6, 7-27' + walkway between 6 and 7 + entrance Row 6 (NO ROWS 1-4); Section 313: '1-3' + entrance Row 3; Section 329: 'Rows in Section 329 are labeled 1-1' + entrance Row 1 (A SINGLE ROW). AGAVE CLUB uses a completely separate scheme, verbatim: 'Standard stadium seating (Rows 1-12)', 'Table seating (TR1-TR3) for small groups', 'Drink rail seating (BR) for fans who prefer bar-style seating'. THE POINT: 'Rows in The Point are labeled 1, SRO' + 'An area named Standing is located behind Row 1' + 'An entrance to this section is located at Row SRO'. THE LANDING and GALLAGHER SQUARE have NO rows at all - The Landing page states 'This is a general admission seating area. Seats and rows are not assigned and are first-come, first-serve.' and Gallagher Square fan reviews use 'Row GA'. ENTRANCE-ROW BEHAVIOUR: RateYourSeats gives an entrance row per section and it VARIES WILDLY - it is at the BACK of the big 100-level sections (Row 39/40/42/44) and at or near the FRONT of the outfield and upper sections (Row 5, 6, 9, 10). RateYourSeats' 'Field Level Down the Line' review explains the former: 'Entry tunnels located at the top of the section leave a very long walk for fans sitting closer to the field.' Sections 13, A and L have NO entrance-row line at all. UPPER-DECK ROW TIERING: 'Upper Box vs Upper Reserved: Rows 1-6 are Upper Box, while rows above Row 6 are Upper Reserved.' 100-LEVEL ROW TIERING: a RateYourSeats expert answer names the two portions - 'the Field Reserved portion of the section (Rows 25 and lower)' and 'the Field Pavilion portion of the section (Rows 27 and higher)'. SEATS: SEE 'seat1_side_verbatim' - THERE IS AN UNRESOLVED CONFLICT. ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION: UNKNOWN. No source consulted states any WC / WCH / VWC / AC row suffix or any dedicated wheelchair row label at Petco Park. The official Padres accessibility guide names seat CATEGORIES ('Wheelchair Accessible, Semi-Ambulatory, and Transfer Seats') but no row labels and no sections. A View From My Seat tags section 314's rows only generically ('Rows here are tagged with: is accessible'). TickPick makes an unsourced generalisation - 'If you're seeking ADA seating, you'll find accessible rows at the top of most sections throughout the venue.' - which is single-sourced and should not be relied on. The only non-numeric row labels documented anywhere are 'A', 'B' (front rows of lower-outfield sections 126/128), 'BRS' (back of section 128), '1D' (section 115), 'SRO' (The Point), 'TR1-TR3' and 'BR' (Agave Club), and 'GA' (Gallagher Square).
seat1_side_verbatim: *** THIS IS THE LARGEST UNRESOLVED CONFLICT IN THE FILE. TWO CREDIBLE SOURCES AGREE ON THE THIRD-BASE/LEFT-FIELD HALF AND FLATLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ON THE FIRST-BASE/RIGHT-FIELD HALF. *** (1) RATEYOURSEATS, verbatim, character for character including the doubled token 'field/field': "When looking towards the field/field/stage, lower number seats are on the right". This sentence is IDENTICAL on EVERY Petco Park section page checked - verified on 16 pages: 13, 101, 102, 107, 108, 110, 115, 126, 128, 129, 133, 134, 137, 201, 204, 235, 300, 313, 329, A, L and The Point (https://www.rateyourseats.com/petco-park/seating/sections/101 and the corresponding URLs). There is NO variant anywhere in that set - no 'left' version, no single-'field' version. The ONLY page that differs does so by omission: The Landing (https://www.rateyourseats.com/petco-park/seating/sections/the__landing) has no Row Numbers block at all and instead says 'This is a general admission seating area. Seats and rows are not assigned and are first-come, first-serve.' Because RateYourSeats emits the SAME string on the first-base side (101, 107, 115), behind home plate (101, 102, 201, 300), on the third-base side (108, 110), in left field (126, 128, 134), in right field (129, 133, 137) and in the lettered Premier Club (A, L), it is treating seat numbering as running uniformly RIGHT-TO-LEFT (as the fan faces the field) everywhere in the park. (2) PETCO PARK INSIDER, verbatim: "Seat numbers:  In each section, Petco seat number 1 will be the closest to home plate. So, if you are sitting on the 1st base (right field) side, seat number 1 will be the leftmost. If seated on the 3rd base / left field side, seat number 1 will be the rightmost." (https://www.petcoparkinsider.com/padres-seating-chart). THE TWO RULES AGREE on the third-base/left-field half (both put seat 1 on the fan's right) and are EXACTLY OPPOSITE on the first-base/right-field half (RateYourSeats: right; Petco Park Insider: left). (3) CORROBORATION FOR THE THIRD-BASE HALF (both rules agree here, so this does not break the tie): a RateYourSeats expert answer on the Section 110 page (110 is EVEN = third base) says verbatim: 'Seat 1 will be on the aisle at the right side of Section 110 as you face the field, putting you closer to home plate. Higher numbered seats will conversely be closer to the left field wall.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/petco-park/seating/sections/110). (4) A FIELD-OBSERVED DATA POINT THAT FAVOURS PETCO PARK INSIDER'S 'SEAT 1 NEAREST HOME PLATE' FORMULATION, on the LEFT-field side where both rules coincide: RateYourSeats fan feedback on Section 134 - 'The Padres Bullpen is to the Left of Section 134 - Sit close to Seat 12 in Section 134 to be near the Padres bullpen.' Section 134 is the outermost even/left-field section and the bullpens sit beyond it toward left-center, so high seat numbers point AWAY from home plate there, i.e. seat 1 is nearest home plate. (5) A THIRD SOURCE THAT CONTRADICTS ITSELF WITHIN TWO PARAGRAPHS - TickPick: 'The Petco Park seating chart with seat numbers indicates that seat 1 is typically located closer to the lower-numbered adjacent section. For example, seat 1 in section 118 would be closest to the highest numbered seat in section 116 (since sections are numbered in even and odd sequences).' (this implies seat 1 nearest home plate on BOTH sides, agreeing with Petco Park Insider) but then 'Typically, the best seats are closer to home plate. Going by that logic, if you're on the left-field line, you'd want a seat with a lower seat number, and on the right-field line, you'd look for a higher seat number.' (this implies the reverse on the right-field side, agreeing with RateYourSeats) (https://www.tickpick.com/blog/san-diego-padres-seating-chart-with-seat-views). NOT RESOLVED HERE. Both primary rules are recorded verbatim; whichever is adopted, the first-base/right-field half of the ballpark is the half at risk.
known_obstructions: PROTECTIVE NETTING - PREFER THE OFFICIAL PADRES LIST. https://www.mlb.com/padres/ballpark/netting states, verbatim: 'There is some amount of netting or screening in front of the following seating sections; the height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section:' / 'All Lexus Home Plate Club sections. Field VIP: Field VIP 101-106. The full square net coverage is also from Sections 109-110 while angled net coverage is from Sections 111-115 on the first base side and Sections 112-116 on the 3rd base side.' / 'Fans in these sections are still exposed to objects leaving the field of play, including bats and bat fragments, and thrown or batted balls; ticket holder assumes all risk of injury. For more information on netting or screening coverage and seating options, please contact the San Diego Padres ticket office at 619 795-5555.' So officially: ALL Home Plate Club sections (0-6) + Field VIP 101-106 + full square net 109-110 + angled net odd 111/113/115 (first base) and even 112/114/116 (third base). The 2019 Padres press release describing the extension says verbatim: 'Protective netting at the ballpark will be extended to the end of Section 116 in left field and Section 115 in right field, proactively surpassing the guidelines issued by Major League Baseball. The netting will reach a maximum height of 24-feet before it tapers down along the foul lines. It will be attached to the top of both dugouts, as well as the tops of the walls along the warning track.' and 'all of the protective netting will be replaced with Promats Athletics 1.2 mm Field Green Ultra Cross Knotless Dyneema Netting, a lightweight, open mesh that is dyed green to meet MLB's recommendation to reduce visible impact on those seated behind the netting.' (https://www.mlb.com/press-release/padres-announce-details-of-extended-netting-at-petco-park-268507488). RATEYOURSEATS' FAN-FEEDBACK NETTING NOTE gives a slightly WIDER range and is repeated verbatim across many Petco pages (101, 102, 107, 108, 110, 115, Home Plate Club, First Base VIP Box, Third Base Coach's Box, Shaded & Covered Seats): 'Front of sections 101-116 are behind the netting - There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 101-116. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section. The netting extends past the dugout and down each line.' Petco Park Insider's summary matches the official list and adds a gloss: 'The Padres went even further, extending the netting three sections past the dugouts before it tapers down along each foul line.' (https://www.petcoparkinsider.com/netting-behind-screens). VIDEOBOARD BLOCKED FROM THE LEFT-FIELD LOWER SEATS: RateYourSeats' Lower Level Outfield review, verbatim - 'The one downfall however is the near impossible views of the main videoboard.' (the main board is above the LEFT-field seats, so left-field lower-bowl fans are underneath it). RateYourSeats' Upper Box review makes the mirror point: 'Seats on the right field side offer a better view of the main video board in left field, but they also tend to receive more direct sun exposure.' A RateYourSeats expert answer on section 110 adds: 'you may have to turn your head quite a bit to the left to get a good view of the scoreboard located above the left field wall. Your view of the scoreboard won't be obstructed, but from that angle and with the seats facing the pitchers mound, it just requires a bit of effort the see it.' VIDEOBOARD LOCATION AND SIZE, Wikipedia verbatim: 'The left-field HD videoboard, manufactured by Daktronics, was installed in 2015. Measuring 61.2 feet (18.7 m) tall by 123.6 feet (37.7 m) wide'. RateYourSeats venue captions place the two boards by section: 'The scoreboard in right field is located just above sections 227-235 at Petco Park.' and 'The left field scoreboard at Petco Park is located right above sections 226-230.' HOME-PLATE SIGHTLINE COMPLAINT IN THE RIGHT-FIELD LOWER BOWL: a RateYourSeats fan review on Section 129 (odd = right field) reads, verbatim - 'Obstructed view of home plate. - Sat in plenty of different seats at Petco and these are the worst by far. Miserable.' (Sec 129 / Row 17). LONG WALKS / TRAFFIC RATHER THAN OBSTRUCTION: RateYourSeats' Field Level Down the Line review - 'The sections here are some of the very largest in Petco Park, with as many as 44 rows of seating. Entry tunnels located at the top of the section leave a very long walk for fans sitting closer to the field.'; a fan review on Section 108 - 'There's traffic going by in front of you and it took awhile to get used to, especially the vendors. Just over enough that you aren't looking through safety screen.' CONCERT-ONLY SIGHTLINE LIMITS (do NOT apply to baseball): RateYourSeats flags 'Behind/Side Stage (most shows)' and prints, e.g., '133 is behind the stage or to the side of the stage for most concerts. This may restrict or limit your view of the performance.' - the same note appears for 134, 137, 235, The Point and The Landing. GALLAGHER SQUARE SIGHTLINES: 'Limited Game Views: Views into the stadium are minimal and depend on where you set up.' / 'Views of the game from Gallagher Square are limited compared to traditional seating sections.' SECTION 314 (Skyline Patio) FRONT-ROW GLASS: A View From My Seat fan note - 'this front row is up against the wall and little piece of one-foot glass.' NO POLE OBSTRUCTIONS were reported by any source. SUN, not obstruction, is the dominant Petco Park seating complaint - see the extensive quotes under 'orientation'.
uncertain: SEAT-1 SIDE CONFLICT (HIGHEST PRIORITY - resolve before generating any seat-1 statement). RateYourSeats says 'When looking towards the field/field/stage, lower number seats are on the right' uniformly on EVERY Petco Park section page checked (22 pages verified, no variation). Petco Park Insider says 'In each section, Petco seat number 1 will be the closest to home plate. So, if you are sitting on the 1st base (right field) side, seat number 1 will be the leftmost. If seated on the 3rd base / left field side, seat number 1 will be the rightmost.' The two rules COINCIDE on the third-base/left-field half and are EXACTLY OPPOSITE on the first-base/right-field half. The only per-section corroboration found (RateYourSeats' expert answer for Section 110 and the fan note for Section 134) is on the third-base/left-field half, where both rules agree, so it does NOT break the tie. COMPASS ORIENTATION IS WELL-SOURCED BUT WORTH RESTATING BECAUSE IT INVERTS THE USUAL MLB ASSUMPTION. Petco Park's batter faces DUE NORTH, not the usual northeast. Consequently the THIRD-BASE side is WEST (shade side) and the FIRST-BASE side is EAST (sun side) - the opposite of the more common arrangement. Two independent sources state it (Wikipedia 'at Petco the batter faces due north'; RateYourSeats 'Petco Park faces north'), and Petco Park Insider explains why ('repositioned slightly toward the north (instead of the more common north-east)' to accommodate the Western Metal building). Gate geography agrees. High confidence, but any code that assumes a northeast-facing default must be overridden for this park.

RATEYOURSEATS' FIELD BOX ZONE RANGE (101-112) CONFLICTS WITH ITS OWN DUGOUT STATEMENT. The zone page says 'Field Box seating at Petco Park includes Sections 101 through 112, located along the infield between the bases' while also saying 'Sections 107-109 sit closest to the Padres dugout, while Sections 108-110 are near the visitor dugout' - i.e. the range 101-112 spans both sides via the odd/even split, not a contiguous arc. This is consistent once the odd/even rule is applied, but any code that treats '101-112' as a contiguous left-to-right arc will place sections wrongly.
